source: post-hoc slice of evidence/o02_paired_bootstrap.json restricted to the 7 combinational designs (21 pairs = 7 designs x 3 seeds), excluding the 3 sequential designs (accu, LFSR, JC_counter) where the KR-1 deterministic-allocator falls back to zero-kill due to absent golden-testbench.
purpose: Sensitivity analysis: does the STRADDLING full-grid CI for (co-evolve - deterministic-allocator) reflect a real inconclusive comparison, or does it reflect KR-1 baseline collapse on the sequential slice? Slicing to combinational-only removes the broken-baseline subsegment and reports the paired-bootstrap CI on the remaining 21 pairs.

comparison.verdict: FIRES on combinational-only slice — co-evolve strictly dominated by deterministic-allocator (upper CI < 0)

interpretation: The full-grid STRADDLE [-0.340, +0.033] is driven by the 3 sequential designs where KR-1 zero-kills; when restricted to the 7 combinational designs where KR-1 is not broken, the CI upper bound moves from +0.033 to -0.0488. The negative-result finding is therefore not an artifact of a broken baseline on 30% of the corpus — it holds on the slice where the baseline is well-defined.
reproduction: Re-run scripts/populate_ledger.py with --restrict-to-combinational flag (or subset o02_e1_aggregate.json.<system>.per_cell arrays to designs matching /^rtllm::(adder|comparator|multi|sub)/ and re-bootstrap 1000x paired).
status_post_amendment_5: The full-grid (co-evolve - deterministic-allocator) CI on 30 pairs is now FIRES [-0.7423, -0.1994] as of 2026-08-22 (freeze_amendment_5 routes KR-1 sequential to formal miter). This combinational-only slice remains valid as a robustness sensitivity check confirming the effect holds when restricted to the 21 combinational-design pairs, but the paper's central claim no longer depends on the combinational-only slice — it fires on the full grid outright.
